== C. AN INDEX IN AN ARGUMENT SLOT -- wherever the callee, whichever spelling.
   A `finfo` field IS a value and a `T.tx_shl` shift amount IS a value, so this
   over-matches BY DESIGN and every hit is read against its callee's parameter.
   It prints the callee precisely so over-matching costs a reader nothing.

   ⚠ THIS SECTION USED TO HAVE TWO BLIND VARIANTS AND BOTH ARE NAMED, because a
   number that cannot see a variant is worse than a number that is small.
     C-i   THE SPELLING. The test was `if "O.Found.i(" in body`, so an index
           routed through a local -- `+m = O.Found.i(s)`, then
           `dd_band(O.Found.ar(s), v, m)` -- was invisible. Same index, other
           spelling.
     C-ii  THE WHITELIST, WHICH IS THE DOMINANT ONE. The window was
           `H.i64_of_i32|H.i64_sub|U32.\w+|T.tx_powi|T.tx_powi32|T.exponent_bias`,
           so an index passed to ANY OTHER callee was invisible whatever its
           spelling. MEASURED on .agents/slop/dd-mutations.frozen.bend: section A
           reports `suspect 7` index-valued `dd_band` mask arguments and the old
           window reached NONE of them, because `dd_band` is not one of the six.
           A NAME WHITELIST IS A FIXTURE LIST: it is stale the moment someone
           writes `dd_band` instead of `dc_band`, which is exactly what happened
           when `dtype.bend` was renamed. Section A reads the ARGUMENT and is
           the one to trust.
   So the old `hard hits: N` was a floor over (six callees) x (one spelling),
   presented as a count. On today's dtype.bend it printed 0, and 0 is ALSO what a
   routed-through-a-local index prints, so 0 was never a clean bill of health.
   Assertion: .agents/slop/formblind-audit.py A13.
